title: Fly visual cell types with more variable input wiring had more variable flicker responses, but cell-to-cell sign variation in wiring did not predict response sign variation (40 types, two connectomes)
abstract: We tested if cell-to-cell variation in the wiring of a fly visual cell type agrees with cell-to-cell variation in its light responses. Wiring came from four optic lobes of two connectomes (FlyWire v783 and male CNS v1.0). Responses came from full-field flicker calcium data of Currier and Clandinin (2025): 369 cells from 60 flies. The test set had 40 types with at least 3 imaged cells from 2 or more flies. The planned primary test was null. The fraction of cells whose modelled signed drive from photoreceptors was against the type sign did not predict the fraction of imaged cells with the opposite ON or OFF sign (Spearman rho -0.06, p 0.66; partial rho 0.16, p 0.17, with control for response quality and mean drive). Wiring heterogeneity was a stable type property: it agreed between hemispheres and between the two connectomes (rho 0.59 to 0.92). In a planned secondary test, types whose cells differ more in input-type mixture, after removal of synapse sampling noise, had less similar responses across flies (rho 0.52; partial rho 0.46, p 0.002). Post hoc checks kept 0.37 to 0.48 with more controls. Single hemispheres gave 0.31 to 0.33, and a permutation inside broad cell classes gave p 0.078. Limitations: anatomy and activity come from different animals, there are few imaged cells per type, the activity data are trial means, and the H3 checks are post hoc. The results are type-level associations, not a cell-level mechanism.
